title: Tenant quota misclassification causing sudden 429s for multi-tenant Dedicated clusters
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Summary:
Customer reported repeated 429 responses from a Dedicated cluster starting 2026-03-09 17:12 UTC. Affected tenants saw sudden token drain and unauthorized quota enforcement even though they had reserved burst capacity. The issue affected both Dedicated and a small percentage of Hosted requests routed through the same quota service; Private deployments with local quota sync saw similar failures in staged upgrades.

Root cause hypothesis (current):
During a quota-store shard migration that ran as part of a background reconciliation (recent change in runtime-2.3), the in-memory tenant->quota mapping could be swapped while the rate limiter continued to reference an old shard id. When the migration completed, the reconciliation job created a new token-bucket object for some tenant IDs but the request routing lookup returned the pre-migration shard id for a short window (~20-40s). This produced a misclassification where requests hit a different token-bucket with a strict committed rate, causing apparent immediate throttling despite customer-configured burst allowances.

Why it's critical:
- High error rate for affected tenants (observed 20-60% error spikes).
- Breaks SLOs for Dedicated customers with reserved capacity.
- Risk of cascading retries causing capacity pressure on fallback variants.

Repro steps (dev):
1) Deploy runtime-2.3 candidate with shard migration enabled to a staging Dedicated cluster.
2) Seed two tenant IDs that will be moved between shards by the reconciler.
3) Simultaneously run a sustained traffic generator that exercises burst windows and collects per-tenant token-bucket metrics.
4) Trigger manual reconciliation and observe transient mismatch between routing lookup and token-bucket owner for the same tenant ID.

Proposed fix (short-term):
- Change the migration sequence to: 1) create new token-bucket objects, 2) atomically update tenant->shard mapping in the central store, 3) then swap in-memory shard index. This ensures routing lookup never returns a mapping without a corresponding token-bucket.
- Add a conservative fallback in the rate limiter: if a lookup fails to find a token-bucket or finds an unexpected owner, fall back to the tenant's previous bucket (if available) for 60s rather than failing closed.
- Add reconciliation audit logs and metrics: mapping-swap latency, orphaned-token-bucket counts, and bucket-mismatch events.

Long-term changes:
- Harden the quota service with transactional migration primitives and unit/e2e tests for migration edge cases.
- Add canary gating so shard migrations only proceed when token-bucket health signals are green.
- Add an automated repair job that reconciles token counts for tenants with suspicious reset patterns and emits customer-facing reports.

Rollout plan:
1) Push patch to runtime-2.3.1 branch and open PR.
2) Canary to a single non-critical Dedicated cluster for 24h with heavy synthetic load (monitor token-bucket mismatch and 429s).
3) If green, roll to remaining Dedicated clusters over 48h with per-cluster validation.
4) Coordinate with Hosted ops to deploy the patch to quota service instances handling multi-tenant routing.
5) For Private customers in staged upgrade windows, provide the patch and migration guidance; offer to run the repair job.

Customer communication:
- Outbound email templates prepared for affected accounts (apology, root-cause summary, remediation timeline, credit offer).
- Priority support bridge for the top 5 affected customers until rollback/repair completes.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests added for migration ordering invariants.
- Integration test that simulates concurrent mapping swap + live requests.
- Load test to ensure no regressions in latency when fallback is exercised.

Monitoring changes:
- New Grafana dashboard panels: per-tenant bucket-owner, mapping-swap-duration, mismatch-rate, and repaired-tenant-count.
- Alerts: mismatch-rate > 0.5% for 5m triggers PagerDuty P0.

Notes about scope across Hosted/Dedicated/Private:
- Dedicated: highest priority due to reserved capacity SLAs. Will be first to canary.
- Hosted: _shared_ quota service nodes require coordinated rollout (ops lead: Marcus Chen).
- Private: provide guidance and optional repair script; most customers will need hands-on support during upgrade.
